ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: this is an automated ruling, made without human review; either of you may appeal it once under POL-GEN-04. The rider's charge of $83.42 is refunded in full.

WHAT THE TRACE SHOWS. The trip is TRP-02823, booked from Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 to Blk 7 Everton Park. The platform's optimal route was 2.4 km / 5.0 min. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02823) records 67.2 km driven. Under POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs, because the trip record's 67.2 km is a rounded copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for the threshold test. The excess is therefore 64.8 km, or 2700% of optimal: both establishment tests (above 20% and above 0.8 km) pass, and the excess is also above the 50% and 8.0 km materiality tests. The deviation is ESTABLISHED and MATERIAL, and the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 (matching trip identifiers and a qualifying excess) is met on the trip record, trace and fare breakdown, which all carry TRP-02823 and the same 08:28:00 trip start.

TRACE INTEGRITY. The trace is clean for policy purposes: 610 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s. None of POL-RD-07(a)-(c) fires, so the deviation stands on the trace alone and needs no independent corroboration.

THE DRIVER'S EXPLANATION. You said the rider changed the destination verbally. POL-RD-04 exonerates a detour only where the rider's instruction is recorded in the chat log, is timestamped before (or within 3 minutes of) the vehicle leaving the optimal corridor, and names a place or road the trace can be tested against via chat_message.waypoint_hint. The chat log for this trip (EV-CHAT-02823) holds zero messages, so there is no instruction, no timestamp and no waypoint_hint; the corroboration test cannot be run, POL-RD-04 is unavailable, and the excess is not reduced. Your statement cites no evidence ID, so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight; and because it cites no artifact, it is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged and the case does not escalate on that ground. No endpoint amendment is recorded (pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null), so POL-RD-05 cannot be run; and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply.

THE REFUND. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs. Recomputed fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 2.4 + 0.28 x 5.0) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP/tolls = 7.80. Refund = 83.42 - 7.80 = 75.62, rounded up to the nearest $0.05 = 75.65, which is 90.6% of the 83.42 charged. Because the refund reaches the 90% full-refund share, POL-RD-02 directs FULL_REFUND rather than a partial, and under POL-GEN-03 a full refund returns the whole contested amount: 83.42. The driver advocate's arithmetic (75.65) is correct and is the POL-RD-02 figure; it is the outcome label, not the arithmetic, that the 90% test changes. The whole charge of 83.42 is returned and the rider's claim for a full refund of 83.42 is accepted.

DRIVER PROFILE. The POL-RD-06 check is required on a material deviation, but deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 210 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established. Neither the POL-RD-06(b) uplift nor the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is available. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not the trailing-90-day field POL-RD-06 names and was not used (POL-GEN-01).

PASS-THROUGH CHARGES. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines, no tolls and no airport surcharge, and the trip neither originates at nor ends at an airport. POL-RD-09 adds nothing on top of the POL-RD-02 figure and there is no billing-integrity finding.

NO ESCALATION. Confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor; the trip identifiers match across the artifacts; no timestamps run backwards; the refund is below both the SGD 150.00 ceiling and the charged total; and no charge line is unmatched. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires. The traffic-advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02823-01 is MISSING (weight 0.00, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); no surviving claim relies on it and no traffic cause was asserted, so it carries no deciding fact and does not cap confidence. Both advocates' claims about that artifact were discarded for citing it without disclosing its impairment.

CONFIDENCE. 0.90, capped by the artifacts that carry the deciding facts - the GPS trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown - each at weight 1.0.

EXECUTION. The monetary effect of $83.42 exceeds the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so the ruling issues but the amount is held for release by a human reviewer under POL-GEN-05.

This is the rider's route-deviation dispute for trip TRP-02823 (21 Aug 2026, Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 to Blk 7 Everton Park). The platform's own records decide it.

Same trip, and the deviation. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02823), the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02823) and the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02823) all carry trip_id TRP-02823 and agree on the pickup and drop-off times, so the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is met. The booked optimal route is 2.4 km (trip_record.optimal_distance_km). The trace - 610 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s - measures the route actually driven at 67.2 km (gps_trace.trace_distance_km). POL-RD-01 makes that figure, not the trip record's rounded copy, the governing one; here they agree. The excess is 64.8 km, 2,700% of optimal. It passes both establishment tests (over 20% and over 0.8 km) and both materiality tests (over 50% and over 8.0 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED and MATERIAL. Both advocates' distance claims are accepted.

Trace integrity. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: there is no gap over 90 s, no jump over 500 m and no sampling interval over 30 s. The deviation therefore stands on the trace alone; POL-RD-10(3) and the POL-RD-07(ii) corroboration requirement are not engaged, as both sides correctly state.

The driver's explanation. The driver's counterparty statement is that 'the rider changed the destination verbally'. That is a rider-instruction excuse, and POL-RD-04 requires the instruction to be recorded in the chat log with a time, and the trace to pass within 200 m of the waypoint the platform resolved into chat_message.waypoint_hint. The chat log for this trip (EV-CHAT-02823) holds 0 messages, so there is no rider instruction, no timestamp and no waypoint to test: the corroboration test could not be run and POL-RD-04 is unavailable. The driver cited no evidence ID for the assertion, and POL-RD-08 gives an assertion citing no evidence no weight; it is discarded as an explanation of the 64.8 km. No endpoint was amended (pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null), so POL-RD-05 cannot be run, and the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The booked 2.4 km optimal stands.

The refund. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs. Read off EV-FARE-02823: charged_total 83.42; surge_multiplier read from the fare breakdown is 1.0; recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 2.4 km + 0.28 x 5.0 min) x 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 7.80. Refund = 83.42 - 7.80 = 75.62, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 75.65, which is 90.6% of the charged total. The rider's own profile does not trigger the corroboration requirement in POL-RD-08: deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the 4-or-more threshold is not met and the claim needs no corroboration beyond the trace. The rider's no_show_disputes_30d of 1 is a different category's counter and is not a ground of decision here.

The trip record and the GPS trace describe the same trip: both carry trip_id TRP-02823, the trace runs from the recorded trip_started event at 2026-08-21T08:28:00+08:00 to the recorded trip_completed event at 2026-08-21T10:09:30+08:00, and the fare breakdown is billed against the same trip_id. The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is therefore met on matching identifiers and timestamps.

The excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on both limbs. The governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 67.2 km, not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km copy, and the booked optimal is 2.4 km, so the excess is 64.8 km — 2700% of optimal, far above both the 20% and 0.8 km establishment tests and above the 50% / 8.0 km materiality tests. The deviation is ESTABLISHED and MATERIAL.

The trace is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 610 fixes at a 10 s sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, so none of limbs (a) to (c) fires. The deviation therefore stands on the trace alone and needs no independent corroboration, and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The driver's only explanation is his counterparty_statement that 'the rider changed the destination verbally'. That is an assertion of a rider-requested detour, and POL-RD-04 requires it to be recorded in the chat_log with a rider-authored, timestamped instruction identifying a place or road, corroborated by the trace passing within 200 m of chat_message.waypoint_hint. The chat log for this trip holds 0 messages, so there is no instruction, no waypoint_hint and no timestamp: the POL-RD-04 corroboration test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable.

No traffic advisory covers this trip window: EV-ADVIS-02823-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and no closure-adjusted optimal exists. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's traffic excuse, if any, carries no weight, and the deviation stands at the measured figure against the booked optimal route.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-ADVIS-02823-01 at weight_multiplier 0.0 but does not name its issue code(s): MISSING_ARTIFACT

ledger.claim: No relocation clause rescues the driver either: trip_record.pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, original_pickup and original_dropoff are null, and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 has no amendment to re-quote against and the booked 2.4 km optimal stands.

The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs. charged_total is 83.42; recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 2.4 + 0.28 x 5.0) x 1.0 surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = 7.80; refund = 83.42 - 7.80 = 75.62, rounded up to 75.65. That is 90.6% of charged_total, so under POL-RD-02 the outcome is FULL_REFUND rather than a partial.

The driver's profile does not establish a repeat-deviation pattern under POL-RD-06: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 210 completed_trips_90d, so neither the 3-or-more limb nor the 0.05 ratio limb is met. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not the trailing-90-day field this clause names and may not be substituted for it. No POL-RD-06(b) uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) referral is available on this record.
flags: context-only profile field mentioned in claim text: prior_deviation_flags

ledger.claim: The rider's profile likewise raises no POL-RD-08 corroboration hurdle: deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the 4-or-more trigger does not fire and the claim is not required to bring evidence beyond the trace.

No ERP or surcharge correction is due: the fare breakdown carries zero ERP lines, zero tolls and zero airport surcharge, and the trip neither originates at an airport nor crosses a gantry, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing on top of the POL-RD-02 figure and there is no billing-integrity defect to refer.

The refund of 75.65 is below the SGD 150.00 ceiling in POL-RD-10(6) and below charged_total, the trip identifiers match across all three artifacts, no timestamps run backwards, and no exculpatory clause has been invoked against a cited artifact — the driver cited no artifact at all. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires and the case can be ruled on the money.
